title: Fruit Into Baskets
statement: Trees in a row each bear one fruit type. You have two baskets, each holding a single type. Starting anywhere, pick one fruit from each consecutive tree going right until you meet a third type. Return the most fruit you can collect.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(15)
    return [[r.randint(0, 9) for _ in range(100000)]]

hints.1_question: This is the longest subarray with at most 2 distinct values. What do you need to track about the current window?
hints.2_nudge: Keep counts of each fruit type in the window. When a third type appears, move the left edge until one type disappears.
hints.3_big_hint: Add fruits[right]; while len(count) > 2: decrement fruits[left]; delete the key if it reaches 0; left += 1. Update the best length.

known_bugs.name: never deletes a type when its count hits zero
known_bugs.followup: A type with count 0 is no longer in your baskets. Does `len(count)` still say so?

known_bugs.name: restarts the window at the new tree
known_bugs.followup: When the third type appears, do you lose the whole run behind you, or can some of it still be reused (for example the most recent repeated type)?

known_bugs.name: allows three types (> 3)
known_bugs.followup: How many baskets do you have? How many types does your window allow?

followups: How would you generalize this to k baskets?
Why can the dictionary never hold more than 3 keys?
